The image displays a plant leaf with several distinct lesions. These spots are irregular in shape, with dark brown or blackish edges and lighter, tan or necrotic centers. Some of the spots appear to have coalesced, forming larger dead areas. The lesion at the tip of the leaf shows significant decay, and some of the dead tissue appears to be breaking away. This pattern strongly matches the description of Anthracnose, which states, "Spots start small, black, and irregular on leaves, expanding into large dead areas that dry and fall out." The other descriptions do not fit. It is not Sooty_Mould as there are no dark, superficial fungal deposits. It is not Die_Back, as the primary symptom is leaf spots, not twig dieback or leaf roll. The symptoms also do not match Powdery_Mildew, as there is no white, powdery growth. Therefore, Anthracnose is the most likely classification.
